## Summary (Ask Bunkankun 聞分館君)

A one-fascicle *fànzàn* 梵讚 (Skt. *brahma-stotra* or *vandanā*) on Avalokiteśvara, prefaced in the Taishō text by an imperial *yùzhì* preface from **Míng Tàizōng wénhuángdì** 大明太宗文皇帝 ([朱棣](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E6%9C%B1%E6%A3%A3), Yǒnglè 永樂, r. 1402–1424) — the *Guānyīn zàn* 觀音讚 — that was added when the work was incorporated into the Yǒnglè-bĕi 永樂北 / Yǒnglènán 永樂南 *zàng* in the early fifteenth century. The translation itself is by **Fǎxián** ([法賢](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E6%B3%95%E8%B3%A2)), the post-989 designation of **Tiānxīzāi** [天息災](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E5%A4%A9%E6%81%AF%E7%81%BD), in the late Sòng *Yìjīng yuàn*.

**Abstract**

The hymn proper is a relatively short Sanskrit-style *stotra* opening with refuge in the bodhisattva, then a sequence of epithets — *padma-pāṇi* (蓮華手), *abhaya-dada* (施無畏), *karuṇā-mūla* (悲根本) — and closing with a request for the bodhisattva's protection. The "梵讚" of the title indicates that the underlying text was understood by the translation bureau to be a proper Sanskrit *stotra* in *brahma-* register (i.e., metrical, classical, learned), as opposed to the more vernacular *gāthā* style used in many *yíguǐ*. Sanskrit parallels are unidentified in any extant Indic manuscript collection; comparison with the [KR6j0252](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6j/KR6j0252) *Gōngdé zàn* (Dānapāla, [施護](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E6%96%BD%E8%AD%B7)) suggests the two derive from related but not identical Sanskrit manuscript exemplars circulating in late-tenth-century North India. With [KR6j0252](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6j/KR6j0252) and [KR6j0253](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6j/KR6j0253), this hymn forms a small *Yìjīng yuàn* corpus of Avalokiteśvara hymnic literature.
